cim_eredeti: Libya deploys artificial intelligence to accelerate agenda 2063 implementation
szoveg_eredeti:
Libya has opened its Third Training Programme on Domesticating Agenda 2063 through artificial intelligence (AI), as the country seeks to strengthen national reporting, data governance and evidence-based decision-making to accelerate the implementation of the African Union’s development blueprint.

The programme, launched in Tripoli this week, brings together data governance, alignment, analysis and national reporting, with a focus on translating continental commitments into measurable national outcomes.

Libya recorded an overall performance of 84% in its national Agenda 2063 implementation report, providing a foundation for the next phase of its implementation efforts.

The priority, according to the African Union Development Agency-NEPAD (AUDA-NEPAD), is now to turn plans into delivery by making every figure verifiable, accelerating reporting and ensuring that decisions are informed by reliable evidence.

Opening the programme, Dr. Ziad Elhajjaji, Minister of State for Digital Economy and Artificial Intelligence, highlighted the transformative potential of responsible AI, trusted data and human judgement in helping institutions plan better, report faster and serve citizens more effectively.

Dr. Mohamed Al-Fadil Gubran, Chairman of Libya’s Permanent Committee for Monitoring and Implementing Agenda 2063, described the country's 84% performance as “a milestone not a finish line” and called for stronger national systems and capacity to ensure that every number can be verified, explained and trusted.

Representing AUDA-NEPAD, Director of Operations Ola Ehinmoro reaffirmed the Agency’s commitment to supporting Libya beyond alignment and into delivery.

He emphasised the importance of capable institutions and reliable data in translating continental commitments into results that people can see and feel in their daily lives.

The training programme is using alignment maps, AI-assisted reports and live dashboards to strengthen Libya's capacity to monitor and report progress under Agenda 2063.
